Destination parentheticals correctly used: plain '*(Claude Code)*' for six blocks, '*(Claude Code, final move of the module)*' for the send-off (context-annotated form, matches spec). No 'copy →' prefix, no '*(end of prompt)*' closer, no blockquote/backtick/naked-indent wrapping anywhere. The two '/rename' fences (L9-11, L115-117) carry no '**Prompt**' label at all — they are slash-command instructions shown as bare code, a different widget than a chat Prompt block, and correctly outside this rule's scope.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1 anchors to 'task.md' (fixed, well-known worktree-root file) — deterministic path. The Phase-5 send-off references the reference/plan.md pair by back-reference plus an explicit discovery instruction ('find them by listing the worktree') rather than a hard-coded path, which is the correct design given the paths were proposed dynamically in an earlier, now-inaccessible (fresh-session) conversation — not an invented alias, and not the harmful 'if file doesn't exist, create it' filler-fallback the rule warns against.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chained-prompt isolation — don't leak downstream pipeline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P2's closing line ('End with: which of the three was the DOMINANT failure mode? You'll build the verifier against that one.') names the STAKES of the Phase-1 choice without pre-solving, deferring, or naming Phase 3's verifier menu — it does not match any of the three listed leak shapes (pre-grill, defer-hard-choice, invoke-named-skill-early). P3 explicitly refuses to pre-name frameworks/practitioners ('Don't name frameworks or practitioners by label. Walk from the specific failure to the specific validation.'), which is deliberate isolation, not a leak.

rules_evaluated.evidence: The only '/clear' offer sits at a genuine phase/session boundary (Phase 5's session-choice), not mid-phase, and is safe by design: the file's own text confirms the downstream prompt does not depend on scrollback either way ('the re-send prompt below stands alone: Claude finds the packaging in the worktree and reads it cold', L127).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Minimal hand-off + Claude self-augments for send-off prompts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The Phase-5 final prompt carries all four required sections in order: (1) Task+paths — 'Run the task at ./task.md using the packaging in this worktree...'; (2) Rules — explicit 'Rules: run the verifier per plan.md cadence; don't paper over failures; if you get stuck, write into RUN-NOTES.md...; I'm walking away.'; (3) Self-augment invitation — 'Then ask for or write anything else you want for the session.' (near-verbatim match to the rule's own example wording); (4) Report-back — the three-list report shape. Textbook match.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P4 ('Show me the verifier before you save anything; I'll push back, then we save.') and P6 (grill-before-lock-in) both use pre-confirm, but both fall under the more specific check_prompts.md §20 grill-before-save requirement for assembled load-bearing artefacts built while the student is still in the room — a rule that explicitly mandates this shape. The one true side-effect/autonomous-run prompt (the Phase-5 final send-off, where nobody is present to confirm) correctly uses post-action reporting ('Report back as three lists...'), matching this rule's default. The file differentiates the two contexts correctly rather than applying one pattern uniformly.

The one absolute-looking path in the final fence ('~/.claude/projects/', keyed by CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID) names the Claude Code session-transcript store, a location outside the repo's own CWD structure entirely, not a restatement of the worktree's working directory — outside this rule's target.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read each fence in isolation against realistic student machine state. The cold, fresh-session Phase-5 fence is fully self-contained: it names './task.md', 'this worktree', and 'find them by listing the worktree' without depending on any body callout, and resolves correctly given the Session-widget's documented launch location.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Repeated Q&A -> premature re-edits. Separate iteration from persistence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P6 (the grill-me artefact-assembly prompt) carries all five required elements: (a) explicit write-gate — 'Don't touch either file until I say lock it in.'; (b) sectional-edit instruction — 'use Edit on the changed section, not Write on the whole file.'; (c) batch cadence — 'Ask three questions at a time.'; (d) slowness-watch callout immediately after the fence — the 'Cut the grill when the package is good enough to re-send... push back if the agent rewrites between turns' blockquote; (e) explicit Approve section — '## Approve / Say *lock it in.* The agent writes both files.' Near-verbatim match to the rule's own model language.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P2, P6, and the final send-off (the file's three longest, multi-move prompts) are each split into one paragraph per logical move (task-framing / lens-list / quote-requirement / dominant-failure-ask in P2; reference-spec / plan-spec / file-paths / write-gate / grill in P6; run-coordinates-setup / self-augment / execution / rules / report-back in the final prompt). Read-aloud diagnostic: each natural breath lands at a paragraph break in all three, not mid-clause.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Five of six mid-file lead-in/fence pairs rhyme cleanly on verb and noun-phrase (P2's 'walk the work through three failure-mode lenses' <-> fence's 'read what came back through three failure-mode lenses'; P3's 'walk each diagnosed failure backwards into the validation' <-> fence's near-identical opening; P6's 'assemble both, scoped to the same task' <-> fence's 'Build me two task-scoped artefacts'). The final send-off's lead-in — 'Ask Claude to re-run the same task using the reference, plan.md, and verifier you just built.' — does not mirror the fence's actual opening clause, which is a prerequisite run-coordinates-recording instruction ('Before you start, write a protected block at the top of plan.md...'); the lead-in's own content only appears in the fence's THIRD paragraph ('Run the task at ./task.md using the packaging in this worktree: the reference, plan.md, and the verifier.'). Not the 38a surprise-pedagogy carve-out (no easter-egg maintainer note licenses the mismatch) and not a maintainer-card edit drift (nothing in the maintainer block documents a recent prompt-only edit here) — a structural necessary-prerequisite-first ordering rather than drafting drift, but still a literal opening-clause mismatch on the highest-stakes prompt in the file.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Reorder the lead-in to name the prerequisite first, e.g. 'Ask Claude to record this session's run coordinates, then re-run the same task using the reference, plan.md, and verifier you just built.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Phase 1-4 correctly read as one continuous warm session (opened once at the Phase-1 Session widget, no /clear before Phase 5) — back-references ('the task we ran un-packaged', 'the failure I diagnosed', 'the three failures we just named') resolve to content the AGENT ITSELF produced earlier in this same session's scrollback (its own Phase-1/2 diagnosis output), not a curriculum-coined Phase-heading label the agent never typed, so the §40b warm-does-not-equal-referent-present trap does not fire. Phase 5 correctly reads as cold (new session, or /clear-in-place) and is self-contained accordingly (verified under §34). No parallel-worktree window is used anywhere in this exercise, so §40a does not apply.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-vs-STOP tail ordering — last imperative wins.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The Phase-5 final prompt has no STOP-after-write pattern: its trailing 'Report back as three lists' is a post-run summary, not a gate blocking an earlier write. P4's 'Show me the verifier before you save anything; I'll push back, then we save.' and P6's grill-gate deliberately hold the write pending confirmation — that is the intended check_prompts.md §20 grill-before-save design, not the rule-41 failure mode (an artifact meant to land immediately, accidentally blocked by a trailing STOP).
